lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 5, who showed the Han emperor a new way to make paper in AD 105? (Cai Lun.) Today: the next great inventions of China, under the Tang and Song dynasties.

The Tang dynasty ruled from 618 to 907. Its capital, Chang'an, was one of the biggest cities in the world, with markets full of traders from the Silk Road. Many officials were chosen by hard written exams.

Printing: craftworkers carved a whole page, back to front, into a block of wood, inked it and pressed paper on it. The oldest printed book with a date, the Diamond Sutra, a Buddhist text, was printed in 868.
The Song dynasty ruled from 960 to 1279. About 1040 Bi Sheng made movable type: a small clay block for each character, set out in a frame to print a page, then used again for the next.
Paper money: strings of coins were heavy to carry, so traders swapped paper notes instead. In 1024 the Song government printed the world's first official paper money.
The compass: a needle rubbed on a magnetic stone points north and south. In 1088 Shen Kuo described a needle hung on a silk thread. By about 1100, ships used compasses to find their way at sea.
Gunpowder was found in the 800s by people mixing chemicals while looking for medicines. It was first used for fireworks and signals. Fireworks still light up festivals such as the Lunar New Year.
Try it in the world: make a stamp of your name from blocks and 'print' it on a wall. Then swap two blocks to print a new word, as movable type does. Next: great African kingdoms.

exercises.prompt: Which dynasty ruled China from 618 to 907?
exercises.explain: The Tang dynasty, from 618 to 907, with its capital at Chang'an.

exercises.prompt: Which way does a compass needle point?
exercises.hint: It lines up with the Earth's magnetism.
exercises.explain: North and south: the magnetised needle lines up with Earth's magnetism.

exercises.prompt: The first fireworks came from China.
exercises.hint: Think of what gunpowder was first used for.
exercises.explain: True: gunpowder was first used for fireworks and signals in China.

choices: the oldest printed book with a date
exercises.explain: The oldest printed book with a date, printed from wooden blocks in 868.

exercises.prompt: Who made movable type from clay about 1040?
exercises.hint: He lived under the Song dynasty.
exercises.explain: Bi Sheng, about 1040: a small clay block for each character.

exercises.prompt: Match each invention to what it is.
exercises.hint: Two are about printing; think which one carves a whole page.
exercises.explain: Woodblock: a page carved in wood. Movable type: a block for each character. Paper money: notes. Compass: a needle pointing north.

exercises.prompt: The Tang dynasty ruled from 618 to 907. How many years is that?
exercises.hint: Take the earlier year from the later one.

exercises.prompt: Why was movable type quicker than woodblocks for a new book?
exercises.hint: What happens to a carved page when the book is finished?
choices: the same blocks could be used again
exercises.explain: A carved page is only good for one page; movable type's blocks can be set out again for any page.

exercises.prompt: Why did traders like paper money?
exercises.hint: Imagine carrying 1,000 coins on a string.
choices: it was lighter than strings of coins
exercises.explain: Paper notes were far lighter to carry than heavy strings of coins.

exercises.prompt: Put these in order, earliest first.
exercises.hint: Look at the years: the smaller the year, the earlier.

exercises.prompt: Gunpowder was first found by people trying to make weapons.
exercises.hint: What were they looking for when they mixed chemicals?
exercises.explain: False: it was found by people looking for medicines, and first used for fireworks and signals.

exercises.prompt: How did a compass help sailors?
exercises.hint: How did sailors find their way before?
choices: they could steer when clouds hid the stars
exercises.explain: Sailors used the Sun and stars; with a compass they could keep their course even under clouds.

exercises.prompt: The Diamond Sutra was printed in 868. Bi Sheng made movable type about 1040. About how many years later?
exercises.hint: Take the earlier year from the later one.

exercises.prompt: How were many Tang officials chosen?
exercises.hint: It tested what people knew, not who their family was.
exercises.explain: By hard written exams, so clever people from more families could become officials.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: invented in China, or somewhere else?
exercises.hint: Algebra came from Baghdad; the Maya lived in the Americas.
exercises.explain: In China: paper money, the magnetic compass, movable type. Elsewhere: algebra (Baghdad) and the Maya zero.
